findings.summary: The entry boundary drops every image-only (ItemUpdateType.ImageUpdate) change, including external source-image changes, not only ArrTags-generated ones.
findings.detail: LibraryEventRelevance.TryCreateHint rejects any change whose Origin is LibraryItemChangeOrigin.Image, and JellyfinLibraryEventSource.MapChange sets that origin whenever the ImageUpdate flag is set. This is broader than 'ignore ArrTags-generated internal changes' (architecture section 8, step 2) because Jellyfin's ItemUpdateType is a [Flags] enum and the boundary cannot distinguish an ArrTags publication from an external image change without an in-memory marker or an I/O read, both of which are out of scope for a short handler. The consequence is bounded: badge inputs come from provider metadata, an external image change is picked up by a later work item or fingerprint-driven invalidation (task 6.6), and the worker re-reads the item. The worker documented this explicitly as a known limitation. Not a blocker for 6.1; worth confirming task 6.6 actually covers the external-source-image-change case.

findings.summary: Boundary relevance checks item type and 'any provider enabled' but not configured library scope or the item-type-specific provider.
findings.detail: TryCreateHint requires at least one of SonarrEnabled/RadarrEnabled rather than the provider matching the item type, and it does not check EnabledLibraries. Architecture section 8 step 1 mentions 'an enabled library/item type', but architecture section 8 also requires the worker to 're-read the item and current configuration before processing', so scope and connection resolution are correctly deferred. The bounded event carries no library identity and resolving it would require I/O, which the handler must avoid. Accepted; no correctness or integrity impact, only a small amount of deferred/rejected work.

findings.summary: BoundedWorkHintSink captures QueueCapacity once at DI resolution, so a later QueueCapacity change is not reflected.
findings.detail: CreateWorkHintSink reads ConfigurationSnapshotService.Current.Limits.QueueCapacity when the singleton is first resolved. Dynamic capacity changes are explicitly assigned to task 6.2 by the task scope boundary and the worker report. The sink is a minimal 6.1 primitive; no impact on 6.1 acceptance. Accepted.

findings.summary: JellyfinLibraryEventSource.MapChange XML doc says 'it is not part of the runtime event flow', which is inaccurate.
findings.detail: MapChange is called by OnItemAdded/OnItemUpdated/OnItemRemoved, so it is on the runtime path; the doc comment is contradictory but does not affect behavior or any project documentation. Cosmetic only.
